status: VALIDATED BY THREE RUNTIMES. Every accept-vector was parsed, re-encoded and projected by two protobuf implementations that share no parser with the writer or with each other, and every reject-vector was SEEN failing by all three. A row where the readings disagree is marked `disputed`, carries every reading, and is excluded from a consumer's pass or fail count rather than failing it -- if two conformant runtimes read the same bytes differently, the corpus's job is to say so, not to pick. The vector BYTES are frozen in vectors.sha256 and the build refuses to move them; everything else in this file is a claim about them and is expected to sharpen as more runtimes are asked. `python3 emit/build.py --check` fails if what is committed is not what the generator writes today.

oracles.why_more_than_one: The first version of this corpus generated every vector, every accepted encoding and every projection with upb, and validated every verdict by parsing with upb. One runtime deciding what the right answer is makes that runtime the specification, and on U-map-entry it is the minority: upb drops a map entry carrying an unknown field out of the map and keeps its bytes as an unknown field of the parent, while protobuf-python's pure backend and protobuf C++ both put the entry in the map.

descriptors.difference: the fields a conformant reader is NOT built against. A vector is WRITTEN against the superset and READ against the reader.

reading_this_file.verdict: `agreed` means every oracle asked read the vector the same way. `disputed` means they did not: the row carries every reading, names which runtime produced each, has no projection of its own, and is EXCLUDED from a consumer's pass or fail count rather than failing it.
reading_this_file.accepted_encodings.written_by: who was SEEN writing that form. 'ffi/corpus/emit, the canonical form of ../schema/README.md' means the corpus's own canonical writer; a runtime name means that runtime re-encoded its own reading this way. The two are different claims and this field keeps them apart.
reading_this_file.permutation_accepted: true where two accepted encodings are the same fields in a different ORDER. Protobuf does not fix field order on the wire, so a consumer's re-encoding passes C3 if it is a permutation of an accepted form. SHAPES.md already validates M7/P7.1 that way and the manifest now says so too.
reading_this_file.produce: the slices expected to emit these exact bytes from their own facade.
reading_this_file.consume: the slices expected to parse them. Empty produce is never a gap by default: an unknown field cannot be emitted by a codec that does not know it, and a must-fail vector cannot be emitted at all.
reading_this_file.accepted_encodings: a vector may have MORE THAN ONE valid encoding. A reader must parse every one of them whatever it writes; a producer must write one of them and say which.
reading_this_file.projection: what a reader must SEE. Byte identity against a manifest generated from the same schema that reads it is a weaker oracle than it looks.
reading_this_file.expect: `reject` means a conformant implementation must refuse the vector. The `seen_failing` row names what was watched refusing it.

classes.unknown: README section 10 item 1: fields the reader does not know.
classes.empty: README section 10 item 2 and R6: absent and empty, where offset defects hide.
classes.shape: README section 10 item 3: every field shape, mechanically.
classes.transcode: README section 10 item 4: the transcode pair, both halves.
classes.chunking: README section 10 item 5: distinct tags across a nesting level, and enough elements to force more than one chunk.
classes.malformed: wire a conformant parser must reject. Not one of the five items; the five items are about what must be READ, and a corpus with no vector that must fail has never watched a rejection work.
classes.baseline: the payloads of ffi/schema/generated, by reference. The corpus is a superset of them and does not copy them.

T-enc-lone-high.why: ABI v1 section 6 puts the converting transcoders in the core and section 12.2 makes the pair an obligation. The input is given as UTF-16 code units in this vector's metadata because a Rust String cannot hold an unpaired surrogate, so no content set constructed in Rust produces it; these bytes were produced by CPython, whose str can. Four sites at once because a transcoder wired at only some of its call sites passes a root-only vector.
